symbols.name: The Tree of Life (Kabbalah)
symbols.desc: Ten luminous sefirot linked by twenty-two paths, traced to the Zohar and the medieval book Bahir — the canonical diagram of the Kabbalistic Tree of Life.
symbols.credit: Diagram after the Bahir / Zohar; public domain

symbols.name: Kircher's Tree of Life
symbols.desc: Athanasius Kircher's engraved Tree of Life from Oedipus Aegyptiacus, fusing the ten sefirot with the Tree of Jesse and Egyptian cosmology into a single allegorical system.
symbols.credit: Engraving by Athanasius Kircher, S.J.; public domain

symbols.name: Tree of Jesse (Chartres Rose)
symbols.desc: The Tree of Jesse from the west-rose window of Chartres Cathedral: Christ at the crown, the patriarchs in the branches, and the kings of Judah in the roots — a stained-glass genealogy of salvation.
symbols.credit: Chartres Cathedral glass; public domain (photo C. H. Moore, 1840–1930)

symbols.name: Bernward Doors — Christ on the Tree of Life
symbols.desc: The Bernward Doors, bronze gate of Hildesheim Cathedral: Christ on the Tree of Life, flanked by the Fall in Eden and the Redemption in Gethsemane — an Ottonian statement of the cross as the tree of life.
symbols.credit: Bronze by the workshop of Bernward of Hildesheim; photo © Bishop's Press Office Hildesheim, CC BY

symbols.name: Chi-Rho Page, Book of Kells
symbols.desc: The Chi-Rho page of the Book of Kells, the IHS monogram of the Word wrapped in interlaced vines, knots and tendrils — an Insular gospel book where the living tree becomes woven ornament.
symbols.credit: Book of Kells, Irish scribes; public domain

symbols.name: Adam and Eve under the Tree of Life (Doré)
symbols.desc: Gustave Doré's 'Adam and Eve under the Tree of Life': the serpent on the forbidden tree and the Tree of Life beyond, an engraved illustration from his edition of the Bible.
symbols.credit: Wood engraving by Gustave Doré; public domain

symbols.name: Ishtar Gate & Processional Way
symbols.desc: The glazed-brick lion procession of the Ishtar Gate of Babylon, where sacred trees and lions line the processional way — the garden of Marduk rendered in blue brick.
symbols.credit: Ishtar Gate, Nebuchadnezzar II; photo © 0x010C, CC BY-SA 4.0

symbols.name: Stele of the Vultures
symbols.desc: The Stele of the Vultures: Gudea of Lagash laying out his temple, with a sacred tree and the vultures of the underworld — Sumerian royal iconography of the sacred tree.
symbols.credit: Stele of Gudea, Louvre; photo © Kikuyu3, CC BY-SA 4.0
symbols.artist:
Background: Kikuyu3
Elements: Eric Gaba (User:Sting)

Composite: पाटलिपुत्र (talk) 10:52, 30 April 2020 (UTC)

symbols.name: Thutmose III and the Tree of Heaven
symbols.location: Tomb of Thutmose III, Valley of the Kings
symbols.desc: Thutmose III seated beneath the sycamore (the 'tree of heaven') of Hathor, the goddess of the West — the Egyptian sacred tree of the afterlife in a Theban tomb painting.
symbols.credit: Wall painting, Valley of the Kings; public domain

symbols.name: Buddha beneath the Bodhi Tree
symbols.desc: The Buddha beneath the Bodhi tree at Jamal Garhi: the wheel of dharma turning, the tree of awakening that frames the first sermon — Greco-Buddhist schist sculpture of the Enlightenment.
symbols.credit: Gandharan schist, 2nd c. CE; photo © SpeakingArch, CC BY-SA 4.0

symbols.name: Penglai, the Island of the Immortals
symbols.desc: Penglai, the island of the Immortals rising from the sea, with the peach tree of immortality — a Tang-dynasty tradition of the celestial tree of eternal life in the far-east seas.
symbols.credit: After Li Sixun (Li Po-chun); public domain

symbols.name: Bronze Money Tree (Sanxingdui)
symbols.desc: A bronze Money Tree from the Sanxingdui culture: a three-branched trunk crowned with perched birds, a dragon and jade — a Han-world axis mundi of wealth and the cosmos.
symbols.credit: Bronze, Sanxingdui Museum; photo © Gary Todd, CC0

symbols.name: The Ceiba of Tikal (Axis Mundi)
symbols.desc: The great ceiba of Tikal, the Maya world-tree whose roots drink from Xibalba and whose canopy holds the gods — the living ceiba that the Classic Maya cities grew around.
symbols.credit: Ceiba pentandra, Tikal National Park; photo CC0 (Flickr)

symbols.name: Ghashghai Carpet — Tree of Life Medallion
symbols.desc: A 19th-century Shiraz (Ghashghai) carpet whose central medallion blooms with the Tree of Life, its branches unfurling pomegranates, roses and vine-scroll — the Persian carpet's garden of paradise.
symbols.credit: Shiraz weavers, 19th c.; photo CC0 (Hiart)

symbols.name: Kermanshah Carpet — Tree of Life
symbols.desc: A late-19th-century Kermanshah carpet: a serpentine Tree of Life flanked by the four paradises, its boughs heavy with fruit — the Persian garden-of-Paradise rendered in wool and silk.
symbols.credit: Kermanshah weavers, 19th c.; public domain

symbols.name: Tāne Mahuta, the Great Kauri
symbols.desc: Tāne Mahuta, the great kauri of the Waipoua Forest, the 'Guardian of the Forest' — one of the largest and oldest living trees on Earth, a Māori taonga (treasure) of the world-tree.
symbols.credit: Kauri (Agathis australis), Waipoua Forest; photo CC BY 2.0 (Flickr)

symbols.name: Yggdrasil (Heine)
symbols.desc: F. W. Heine's 'Yggdrasil': the great ash of the Norse cosmos, its branches over the nine worlds, with the dragon NídhoŁgn gnawing the roots — a 19th-century romantic revival of the world-tree.
symbols.credit: Oil by Friedrich Wilhelm Heine; public domain

symbols.name: Yggdrasil (Mundane Tree, Bagge)
symbols.desc: Oluf Bagge's 'Mundane Tree' (Yggdrasil): the ash of the Norse world, the eagle on its crown and the serpent in its roots — a mid-19th-century depiction of the nine-world axis.
symbols.credit: Oil by Oluf Bagge; public domain

symbols.name: Face-Towers of the Bayon
symbols.desc: The face-towers of the Bayon at Angkor, whose serene stone faces look out over the world-tree of the Khmer cosmos — the temple-mountain of Avalokiteshvara as a cosmic tree.
symbols.credit: Bayon temple, Angkor; photo © Arabsalam, CC BY-SA 3.0

symbols.name: St Agatha & the Tree of Life (Monreale)
symbols.desc: Saint Agatha enthroned beneath a Tree of Life in the apse mosaic of the Cathedral of Monreale, the Norman-Byzantine gold ground of paradise.
symbols.credit: Apse mosaic, Monreale Cathedral; photo © José Luiz, CC BY-SA 4.0

symbols.name: St Lawrence & the Tree of Life (Monreale)
symbols.desc: Saint Lawrence and the Tree of Life in the Monreale apse mosaic, a golden garden of paradise set in the Norman-Byzantine gold ground.
symbols.credit: Apse mosaic, Monreale Cathedral; public domain

symbols.name: Sacred Tree & Winged Genii (Nimrud)
symbols.desc: The Assyrian sacred tree flanked by winged genii with pollen cones, from Ashurnasirpal II's Northwest Palace — the palm-like world-axis at the heart of Assyrian royal ideology.
symbols.credit: Alabaster relief, Nimrud; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Cylinder Seal with the Sacred Tree
symbols.desc: A Mesopotamian cylinder seal cut with the sacred tree between gods and beasts — the garden of the gods worn on the wrist, rolled into eternity across clay.
symbols.credit: Cylinder seal impression; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Warka Vase
symbols.desc: The Warka Vase of Uruk: registers of water, grain, sheep and worshippers rising to the goddess Inanna — the oldest carved narrative of the land's abundance climbing like a tree toward heaven.
symbols.credit: Uruk ritual vase, Iraq Museum; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Etana and the Eagle
symbols.desc: The shepherd-king Etana carried heavenward on the eagle's back to fetch the plant of birth — the Mesopotamian ascent myth, stamped in miniature on a cylinder seal.
symbols.credit: Cylinder seal impression; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Tree Goddess (Tomb of Sennedjem)
symbols.desc: The goddess Nut pouring water from the sycamore in the tomb of Sennedjem — the tree-goddess who quenches the souls of the dead at the edge of the western desert.
symbols.credit: Wall painting, Deir el-Medina; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Osiris Bed
symbols.desc: The Osiris bed: a wooden frame sown with grain that sprouts in the dark in the shape of the risen god — the Egyptian tree of death-and-return, greenness itself resurrected.
symbols.credit: Funerary object; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Menorah of Titus' Arch
symbols.desc: The seven-branched menorah carved on the Arch of Titus, carried from the burning Temple of Jerusalem — the menorah as the Tree of Life in exile, its branches remembered in stone.
symbols.credit: Marble relief, Rome; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Tree of Life — San Clemente Apse
symbols.desc: The apse mosaic of San Clemente in Rome: the crucified Christ rises as a vast acanthus Tree of Life, its coils filling heaven with deer, peacocks, shepherds and saints.
symbols.credit: Apse mosaic, Basilica San Clemente; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Tree of Life — Otranto Floor
symbols.desc: The vast 12th-century mosaic floor of Otranto Cathedral: the Tree of Life running the whole nave's length, threaded with Alexander, Arthur, Adam and the beasts of every age.
symbols.credit: Mosaic floor, Otranto Cathedral; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Tree of Jesse Window (Saint-Denis)
symbols.desc: The Tree of Jesse window of Suger's Saint-Denis — the ancestor-tree of Christ bursting into glass and light, the origin of Gothic stained glass itself.
symbols.credit: Stained glass, Saint-Denis; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Green Man
symbols.desc: The Green Man — the foliate face whose mouth pours vines, carved in a thousand churches — the old arboreal spirit folded into the margins of Christian stone.
symbols.credit: Medieval carving; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Mshatta Facade
symbols.location: Qasr al-Mshatta, Jordan (now Pergamon Museum, Berlin)
symbols.desc: The Mshatta facade: a mile of carved vines on the desert palace wall — the endless tree of life of Umayyad stonemasons, animals dissolving into its scroll.
symbols.credit: Carved facade, Pergamon Museum; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Tree of Life Tilework
symbols.desc: Safavid tilework trees — cypresses bending with birds in lapis and turquoise — the Persian garden of paradise fired onto the walls of Isfahan.
symbols.credit: Ceramic tile, Iran; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Tree of Life Silk (Safavid)
symbols.desc: A Safavid silk woven with the Tree of Life — hunters, simurghs and blossoming branches — paradise textile carried along the silk roads as diplomatic gold.
symbols.credit: Woven silk, Safavid; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Ottoman Tree of Life Textile
symbols.desc: Ottoman court weavers' Tree of Life — carnations, tulips and cypresses rising in silk and metal thread — the imperial garden of eternity.
symbols.credit: Woven textile, Ottoman; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Senmurv Silk
symbols.desc: The Sasanian silk with the senmurv — the dog-bird of the tree — circling the pearl-bordered Tree of Life, the royal emblem of a cosmic garden.
symbols.credit: Woven silk, Sasanian; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Garden of Pasargadae
symbols.desc: Cyrus' garden at Pasargadae — the original chahar bagh, four rivers watering a planted paradise — the world's first designed garden as a tree of life in plan.
symbols.credit: Archaeological site, Iran; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Enclosed Garden (Persian Miniature)
symbols.desc: A Timurid miniature of the enclosed garden — blossoming trees, watercourses and lovers — paradise painted as the Persians imagined the soul's destination.
symbols.credit: Manuscript painting; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Kalpavriksha — the Wishing Tree
symbols.desc: Kalpavriksha, the wish-fulfilling tree of Hindu and Jain cosmology — rooted in the churning of the milk ocean, granting every desire that reaches its shade.
symbols.credit: Indian painting; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Great Banyan of Howrah
symbols.desc: The Great Banyan of the Calcutta garden — a single tree become a forest, dropping aerial roots until it covers a quarter-hectare grove — the banyan as immortal tree-of-life made fact.
symbols.credit: Ficus benghalensis, Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose garden; photo CC

symbols.name: Mughal Tree of Life Carpet
symbols.desc: A Mughal carpet flowering with the Tree of Life — flowering plants naturalized with botanist's eyes, the Persian tree re-planted in the gardens of the Great Mughals.
symbols.credit: Woven carpet, Mughal; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Mahabodhi Temple
symbols.desc: The Mahabodhi temple at Bodh Gaya, raised beside the very seat of the Buddha's awakening — the descendants of the original Bodhi tree still shading pilgrims after 2,300 years.
symbols.credit: Brick temple, Bodh Gaya; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Bodhi Tree Worship (Sanchi)
symbols.desc: The aniconic Buddha as the Bodhi tree itself on Sanchi's gateways — worshippers kneeling before an empty throne beneath the leaves, the tree as the Enlightened One.
symbols.credit: Stone torana relief, Sanchi; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Bodhi Tree of Bharhut
symbols.desc: The Bharhut railing carved with the Bodhi tree of Bodh Gaya, worshipped by kings and nagas — the earliest surviving sculpture of the tree of awakening.
symbols.credit: Stone relief, Indian Museum Kolkata; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi
symbols.desc: The Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi of Anuradhapura — a sapling of the Buddha's own tree, carried by the nun Sanghamitta — the oldest documented living human-planted tree on Earth.
symbols.credit: Ficus religiosa, Anuradhapura; photo CC

symbols.name: Borobudur
symbols.desc: Borobudur — the great Javanese stupa as a carved stone mountain, its galleries circling toward emptiness like a walker circling the world-tree to its crown.
symbols.credit: Borobudur temple; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Trees of Ta Prohm
symbols.desc: The strangler figs and silk-cotton trees of Ta Prohm, swallowing the Khmer monastery root by root — the jungle's own tree of life repossessing the temple of the Buddha.
symbols.credit: Tetrameles nudiflora, Angkor; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Xiwangmu, Queen Mother of the West
symbols.desc: Xiwangmu in her western paradise beneath the peach tree of immortality, guarded by the moon-hare and the nine-tailed fox — the Taoist goddess of the immortal orchard.
symbols.credit: Chinese painting; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Jōmon Sugi
symbols.desc: Jōmon Sugi, the primeval cedar of Yakushima's moss-forest — a tree old beyond record, sacred to Shintō since before Japan had a name.
symbols.credit: Cryptomeria japonica, Yakushima; photo CC

symbols.name: Shinboku — the Rope-Bound Tree
symbols.desc: A shinboku, the sacred tree of a Shintō shrine, bound with the rice-straw rope of the kami — the living tree itself as the body of the god.
symbols.credit: Sacred tree with shimenawa; photo CC

symbols.name: The Garden of the Hesperides
symbols.desc: The Hesperides among their golden apples on the tree Ladon guards at the world's western edge — the Greek tree of immortal life, Herakles' eleventh labor.
symbols.credit: Greek vase painting; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Sacred Olive of Athena
symbols.desc: The Erechtheion, sheltering the mark of Poseidon's trident and Athena's sacred olive — the goddess' gift of the tree that made Athens, replanted after the Persians burned it and sprouting again.
symbols.credit: Temple, Acropolis; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Sacred Oak of Dodona
symbols.desc: The oak of Zeus at Dodona, where the god spoke in the rustling leaves and priestesses read the wind — Greece's oldest oracle, a tree that answered.
symbols.credit: Sanctuary of Dodona; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Pakal's Sarcophagus Lid
symbols.desc: Pakal the Great falling down the World Tree to Xibalba and rising as the maize god — the Maya axis mundi carved in one vast limestone lid.
symbols.credit: Sarcophagus lid, Palenque; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Izapa Stela 5
symbols.desc: Izapa Stela 5, the richest of Izapan carvings — a great branching tree with figures on both sides of its waters — called by some the oldest American Tree of Life.
symbols.credit: Izapan stone; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: World Trees of the Codex Borgia
symbols.desc: The folded pages of the Codex Borgia, where four world-trees hold the four directions and the Tlaloques pour the rains — the Mexica cosmos as a grove of colored trees.
symbols.credit: Pre-Columbian manuscript; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Templo Mayor
symbols.desc: The twin temple of Tenochtitlan — war and rain, the eagle's cactus and the serpent — planted at the center of the Aztec world like a tree between earth and sky.
symbols.credit: Aztec temple, Mexico City; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Sun Stone — Axis of the Fifth Sun
symbols.location: Tenochtitlan (now National Museum of Anthropology, Mexico City)
symbols.desc: The Aztec Sun Stone — the fifth sun born at Teotihuacan, its rays ending in solar symbols, the face of the axis around which the Mexica world turned.
symbols.credit: Basalt disk, Mexico City; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Ayahuasca — the Vine of Souls
symbols.desc: Banisteriopsis caapi, the great vine of the Amazon — the 'rope of the dead' that climbs the forest canopy and carries the shaman up the world-tree of vision.
symbols.credit: Malpighiaceae vine; photo CC

symbols.name: Avenue of the Baobabs
symbols.desc: The Avenue of the Baobabs — Adansonia grandidieri giants lining a dirt road in Menabe, the upside-down tree of African myth with its roots in the sky.
symbols.credit: Adansonia grandidieri, Madagascar; photo CC

symbols.name: The Iroko
symbols.desc: The iroko, the great tree of West African religion — home of spirits, altar of Ogun and the ancestors, never cut without sacrifice — the African world-tree standing between the living and the dead.
symbols.credit: Milicia excelsa; photo CC

symbols.name: The Boab
symbols.desc: The boab of the Kimberley, the hollow-bellied prison tree of Dreaming stories — Adansonia gregorii, the ancestral tree of Australia's northwest.
symbols.credit: Adansonia gregorii; photo CC

symbols.name: Crann Bethadh — the Celtic Tree
symbols.desc: Crann Bethadh, the Tree of Life of the Celts — the oak of the druids connecting sky, sea and land, its memory coiled into high crosses and knotwork branches.
symbols.credit: Celtic carving; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Tree of Life (Stoclet Frieze)
symbols.desc: Gustav Klimt's Tree of Life in the Stoclet dining room — the expectant embrace, the golden spiral branches, the only landscape the master ever painted.
symbols.credit: Gustav Klimt, Stoclet Frieze; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Bronze Gates of Balawat
symbols.desc: The bronze bands of Shalmaneser III's gates, repoussé with the sacred tree between campaigns — the Assyrian world-tree marching with the army.
symbols.credit: Bronze repoussé, British Museum; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Treasures of Ur — the Great Death Pit
symbols.location: Royal Cemetery of Ur (now British Museum / Penn Museum)
symbols.desc: The gold, lapis and carnelian of Ur's royal cemetery — trees and rosettes of the Sumerian garden of the dead, dug from the soil between the rivers.
symbols.credit: Sumerian goldwork; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Tree-Goddess Amulet
symbols.desc: A small amulet of the sycamore goddess with her offering vessel — Hathor-Nut of the West, the tree that feeds the dead, carried on the living.
symbols.credit: Egyptian amulet; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Nut, the Sky-Tree Mother
symbols.desc: The sky-goddess Nut arched over the earth, her hands at the western and eastern horizons — mother of the sun who dies in her mouth and is born from her womb as the morning sycamore.
symbols.credit: Tomb painting / papyrus; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Hagia Sophia — the Golden Vine
symbols.desc: The golden vines and verdant marble of Justinian's Hagia Sophia — the Byzantine church as a garden, its columns grown like a forest beneath the dome of heaven.
symbols.credit: Byzantine mosaic and marble, Hagia Sophia; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Transfiguration Apse (Sinai)
symbols.desc: The apse mosaic of Saint Catherine's monastery at Sinai — Christ in a mandorla of light, the bush that burned and was not consumed, rays falling like branches over the prophets.
symbols.credit: Byzantine mosaic, Sinai; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Alhambra — the Walled Garden of Paradise
symbols.desc: The Alhambra's Court of the Lions, water running from the fountain through four rivers of marble — the Nasrid palace as the Quran's garden beneath which rivers flow, carved in stucco groves.
symbols.credit: Nasrid architecture, Granada; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Qur'anic Garden Illumination
symbols.desc: The illuminated borders of the Mamluk and Ottoman Qur'an — gold vines and palm-blossoms growing around the promise of the garden beneath which rivers flow.
symbols.credit: Manuscript illumination; photo public domain / CC
symbols.artist: Ali ibn Muhammad al-Mukattib al-Ashrafi / Ibrahim al-Amidi

symbols.name: Chahār Bāgh — the Persian Paradise Avenue
symbols.desc: The Chahār Bāgh avenue of Safavid Isfahan, a garden-city's spine of plane trees and water — the Achaemenid paradise evolved into a city's tree of life.
symbols.credit: Safavid urban garden, Isfahan; photo CC

symbols.name: The Vajrāsana — Diamond Throne
symbols.desc: The Vajrāsana, the sandstone throne Ashoka placed at the foot of the Bodhi tree — the diamond seat where the earth herself witnessed the Buddha's awakening.
symbols.credit: Mauryan sculpture, Bodh Gaya; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Pine of Longevity
symbols.desc: The bungeana pines of Chinese temples — bark flaked like clouds, bent by centuries into dragons — the pine of longevity planted beside every hall of the immortals.
symbols.credit: Pinus bungeana; photo CC

symbols.name: The Ginkgo — the Living Fossil Tree
symbols.desc: The ginkgo, sole survivor of a genus 200 million years old, planted at Chinese and Japanese temples as the tree of endurance — leaves like golden fans falling at equinox.
symbols.credit: Ginkgo biloba; photo CC

symbols.name: Araucaria — the Sacred Monkey-Puzzle
symbols.desc: The araucaria groves of the Mapuche — pehuen trees of the Andean slopes, sacred to the people who take their name from them, their seeds the bread of the mountain gods.
symbols.credit: Araucaria araucana; photo CC

symbols.name: The Giant Sequoia
symbols.desc: The giant sequoias of the Sierra — the largest living things on Earth, elders of 3,000 years held sacred by the Sierra tribes, each a standing biography of the continent.
symbols.credit: Sequoiadendron giganteum; photo CC

symbols.name: The Western Red Cedar
symbols.desc: The western red cedar, the tree-of-life of the Pacific Northwest coast — the Longhouse Lifegiver from whose body the peoples cut houses, canoes, boxes and totems.
symbols.credit: Thuja plicata; photo CC

symbols.name: The Breadfruit — Tree of Navigators
symbols.desc: The breadfruit carried across the Pacific in canoes — the tree of Bounty mutiny and of island life itself, planted as a blessing for unborn generations.
symbols.credit: Artocarpus altilis; photo CC

symbols.name: The Baobab — the Upside-Down Tree
symbols.desc: The African baobab — the upside-down tree of a thousand folk tales, the tree the gods planted in anger and threw back roots-to-sky — water-hoarding giant of the savanna, home of spirits.
symbols.credit: Adansonia digitata; photo CC

symbols.name: The Stelae of Aksum
symbols.desc: The granite stelae of Aksum, carved like multi-story towers with false doors and beam-ends — stone trees raised over the kings of Ethiopia, roots of a Christian-African world-axis.
symbols.credit: Aksumite stelae; photo public domain / CC
symbols.artist: A. Davey from Where I Live Now: Pacific Northwest

symbols.name: Kanaga Mask of the Dogon
symbols.desc: The Dogon kanaga mask — the cruciform of Amma's creative hand and the falling nommo, danced at dama funerals to complete the tree of the world's order.
symbols.credit: Dogon wood mask; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Coolabah of the Watercourses
symbols.desc: The coolabah, shade-tree of the inland waterholes in Waltzing Matilda country — in Aboriginal tradition the tree of the waters, where the rainbow serpent sleeps beneath its roots.
symbols.credit: Eucalyptus coolabah; photo CC

symbols.name: The Garden Room — Villa of Livia
symbols.desc: The painted garden of Livia's villa — walls dissolved into a birdsong paradise of laurels, pomegranates and cypresses, an eternal spring grown indoors for an empress.
symbols.credit: Roman fresco, Palazzo Massimo alle Terme; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Investiture of Zimri-Lim
symbols.location: Royal Palace of Mari, Syria (now Louvre)
symbols.desc: The wall-painting of King Zimri-Lim and Ishtar beneath date palms and flowing vases — the Mesopotamian sacred tree granting legitimacy to the throne of Mari.
symbols.credit: Old Babylonian mural, Louvre; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Mulberry Tree (Van Gogh)
symbols.desc: Van Gogh's mulberry in the asylum garden at Saint-Rémy — a single tree burning gold against the blue, roots gripping the rock of a world the painter could not keep.
symbols.credit: Vincent van Gogh, 1889; public domain

symbols.name: The Gray Tree (Mondrian)
symbols.desc: Mondrian's early tree — branches dissolving into cubist lattice, the world-tree abstracting toward the vertical and horizontal, a theosophist's Tree of Life losing its leaves to geometry.
symbols.credit: Piet Mondrian; public domain

symbols.name: Red and White Plum Trees (Kōrin)
symbols.desc: Ogata Kōrin's paired plum trees — one austere white, one blooming crimson — across a golden river: the Rinpa master's flat, luminous world-tree in gold leaf and tarashikomi.
symbols.credit: Ogata Kōrin, folding screen; public domain

symbols.name: Old Trees, Level Distance (Guo Xi)
symbols.desc: Guo Xi's ink scroll of ancient trees receding into mist — the literati cosmology in which gnarled pines are elders, mist is breath, and distance itself is a spiritual exercise.
symbols.credit: Guo Xi, handscroll, Metropolitan Museum of Art; public domain

symbols.name: Tree of Life Tapestry (Morris & Co.)
symbols.desc: The Arts and Crafts Tree of Life — William Morris's medievalist vine, coiling acanthus and fruiting boughs woven at Merton Abbey, sacred nature redeemed by the hand of the craftsman.
symbols.credit: Morris & Co. design; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Tree of Life Window (Tiffany Studios)
symbols.desc: The Tiffany Studios Tree of Life — a symmetrical vine in opalescent glass, roots and crown mirroring in leaded light, the American Gothic window become a luminous world-axis.
symbols.credit: Tiffany Studios, leaded glass; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Palampore — the Coromandel Tree of Life
symbols.desc: The palampore — a chintz tree of life drawn and dyed on the Coromandel Coast for the world's beds and altars: one flowering stem rooted in a mound, branching into peacocks, moths and lotus.
symbols.credit: Indian chintz, mordant-dyed cotton; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Árbol de la Vida — Tree of Life Candelabra
symbols.desc: The Metepec tree of life — a clay candelabra flowering with Adam and Eve, mermaids, cactus and doves, the Tree of Eden retold in Talavera color by generations of Mexican family workshops.
symbols.credit: Mexican folk pottery; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Pipal Tree Seal of the Indus
symbols.desc: The unicorn and pipal seals of Harappa — a leaf-veined ficus religiosa standing on a platform above worshippers, the oldest script-less testament to a sacred tree, four thousand years old.
symbols.credit: Indus Valley steatite seal; photo public domain / CC
symbols.artist: Ernest John Henry Mackay (5 July 1880 – 2 October 1943)

symbols.name: The Djed Pillar — Backbone of Osiris
symbols.desc: The djed pillar — four crossbars like a lopped trunk, the backbone of Osiris and the tree-stump of the buried god, raised at the Sed festival to steady the axis of the world.
symbols.credit: Egyptian amulet / relief; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Ardre Image Stone
symbols.desc: The carved slabs of Gotland — Odin, Thor fishing the serpent, and a rider beneath the arch of the world-tree: Viking cosmology chiseled into limestone flagstones that raised the dead.
symbols.credit: Viking picture stone, Gotland; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Cedars of God — Horsh Arz el-Rab
symbols.desc: The Cedars of God — the last ancient grove of the Lebanon cedar, timber of Solomon's temple and Gilgamesh's forbidden forest, a thousand survivors standing in their own sanctuary.
symbols.credit: Cedrus libani; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Olives of Gethsemane
symbols.desc: The eight gnarled olives of Gethsemane — scientifically dated to the era of Christ, their roots older than their trunks, witnesses at the foot of the Mount of Olives.
symbols.credit: Olea europaea, Jerusalem; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Olive Tree of Vouves
symbols.desc: The Monumental Olive of Vouves — a Minoan-era tree still bearing fruit, its hollow trunk a cathedral of grain, the great mother of the Mediterranean's oil-giving tree of life.
symbols.credit: Olea europaea, Crete; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: Shalimar Bagh — the Mughal Paradise
symbols.desc: Jahangir's Shalimar Bagh — terraces of chinar and water falling through marble pavilions along Dal Lake, the Persian chahār bāgh rebuilt in Kashmir as a Quranic garden for an empress.
symbols.credit: Mughal garden, Srinagar; photo public domain / CC

symbols.name: The Totem Pole — Cedar Column
symbols.desc: The totem pole — a western red cedar carved with raven, bear and thunderbird rising crest above crest, the coast peoples' genealogy raised as a living column between earth and sky.
symbols.credit: Pacific Northwest carved cedar; photo public domain / CC
symbols.artist: B.C. Printing & Litho Ltd.Jasper National Park (Alta.): Publisher

symbols.name: Akshaya Vata Tree of Life (Pattachitra)
symbols.desc: Pattachitra scroll painting of the Akshaya Vata, the imperishable banyan of Hindu myth regarded as a Tree of Life that survives the dissolution of the world.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Madhubani Tree of Life
symbols.desc: Hand-painted Madhubani folk art from Bihar with a central tree framed by birds and figures; the tree is a recurring motif of life, fertility and cosmic connection in Mithila painting.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Squirrels in a Plane Tree (Mughal miniature)
symbols.location: British Library, India Office Collections, London
symbols.desc: Mughal miniature by Abu'l Hasan and Ustad Mansur showing squirrels in a flowering plane tree, a celebrated study of a living tree from the Jahangir-era atelier.
symbols.credit: Self-scanned

symbols.name: Krishna Fluting Under a Tree
symbols.desc: Indian miniature of Krishna playing the flute beneath a blossoming tree, from the Edwin Binney 3rd Collection; the flowering tree frames the divine musician as a symbol of living nature.
symbols.credit: Flickr

symbols.name: Buddha Under the Bodhi Tree (10th Karmapa thangka)
symbols.location: Rubin Museum of Art, New York (Karmapa 900 project)
symbols.desc: Thangka by Chöying Dorje, the Tenth Karmapa, depicting Siddhartha beneath the Bodhi Tree on the verge of enlightenment, surrounded by Mara's legions.
symbols.credit: http://www.karmapa900.org/contributions_10th.html
symbols.artist: Chöying Dorje, 10th Karmapa, Photo by Karl Debreczeny

symbols.name: Bodhi Tree Thangka, Weherahena Temple
symbols.desc: Thangka-style painting of the Buddha under the Bodhi Tree at Weherahena Temple in southern Sri Lanka, continuing the iconography of the tree of awakening.
symbols.credit: Self-photographed ,  http://mstyslav-chernov.com/

symbols.name: Kalamkari Tree of Life Textile
symbols.desc: Kalamkari ('pen-work') hand-painted or block-printed cotton textile from Andhra Pradesh, whose temple-cloth tradition features the flowering tree of life amid vegetal scrollwork.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Describing the Doctrine Under a Tree (Dunhuang silk banner)
symbols.desc: Silk banner painting from the Dunhuang caves showing a teacher expounding the doctrine beneath a tree; discovered at Mogao and now in the British Museum.
symbols.credit: 15:04, 4 April 2010 image only: Zhongguo gu dai shu hua jian ding zu (中国古代书画鑑定组). 1997. Zhongguo hui hua quan ji (中国绘画全集). Zhongguo mei shu fen lei qu

symbols.name: Naesosa Dangsan Sacred Tree
symbols.location: Naesosa Temple, Buan County, North Jeolla, South Korea
symbols.desc: The thousand-year-old dangsan namu (sacred village-tree) at Naesosa Temple, honored with ritual offerings as guardian tree linking the human and spirit worlds.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Suhan Village Dangsan Tree
symbols.location: Suhan Village, Gurye County, South Korea
symbols.desc: Dangsan namu, the sacred tree of Suhan Village in Gurye, the focus of the dangsan-je village ritual that honors the tree as dwelling of protective spirits.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Tamagushi (Sakaki Offering Branch)
symbols.desc: A Shinto priest presenting a tamagushi — an offering branch of the sacred sakaki tree (Cleyera japonica) decked with paper shide streamers, the evergreen that invites kami to descend.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Sakaki Votive Offering, Katori Jingū
symbols.desc: Votive offering ensemble at Katori Jingū including a potted sakaki tree with sake, rice and vegetables — the sacred evergreen at the heart of Shinto worship.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Shinbashira (Pagoda Heart-Pillar)
symbols.desc: Diagram of the shinbashira, the freestanding central pillar of a Japanese five-story pagoda; tradition holds it derives from the sacred tree-trunk axis that anchors the tower between heaven and earth.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: The Oath of Omladina under the Slavic Linden Tree (Mucha)
symbols.desc: Alphonse Mucha's poster 'The Oath of Omladina under the Slavic Linden Tree' — the linden (lípa) as national world-tree under which young Slavs swear brotherhood.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Kongo Cosmogram (Dikenga)
symbols.desc: The dikenga dia Kongo or 'Yowa' cross — the Bakongo cosmogram whose rotating sun-cross maps birth, life, death and rebirth around the great axis linking the world of the living with the world of the dead.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Kongo Cosmogram, First African Baptist Church
symbols.location: First African Baptist Church, Savannah, Georgia, USA
symbols.desc: Kongo cosmograms engraved into the floorboards of the First African Baptist Church in Savannah by enslaved Bakongo worshippers — the sacred cross carried across the Atlantic.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Dogon Divination Table
symbols.desc: Dogon divination table, whose fox-tracking cosmology descends from the Dogon creation myth in which the world's order is revealed through signs traced in earth.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: St George Mural, Narga Selassie, Lake Tana
symbols.location: Church of Narga Selassie, Dek Island, Lake Tana, Ethiopia
symbols.desc: Wall painting of St George in the round church of Narga Selassie on Lake Tana; Ethiopian church murals frame holy scenes in lush vegetal borders echoing the paradisal tree.
symbols.credit:
St. George Slaying The Dragon 
 
  Uploaded by  Elitre
symbols.artist: A. Davey  from Where I Live Now: Pacific Northwest

symbols.name: St George Mural, Lalibela Rock Church
symbols.desc: Thirteenth-century rock-cut church painting at Lalibela illuminated by a shaft of sun — part of the mural programme of Ethiopia's monolithic churches.
symbols.credit:
St. George and the Dragon, Lalibela, Ethiopia 
 
  Uploaded by  Elitre
symbols.artist: A. Davey  from Where I Live Now: Pacific Northwest

symbols.name: Iroko Wood Carving
symbols.desc: Carved artwork made from iroko (Milicia excelsa), the tree revered in Yoruba and Igbo belief as the dwelling of powerful spirits and a bridge between earth and sky.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Chichilaki (Georgian New Year Tree)
symbols.desc: The chichilaki, a Georgian New Year tree made of shaved hazelnut or walnut wood curled into a white beard-like canopy, said to represent the beard of St Basil or the tree of life.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Sogdian Mural, Panjakent
symbols.desc: Wall painting from Panjakent, the eastern capital of Sogdia, whose banquet and garden scenes preserve the Iranian sacred-tree and paradise-garden imagery of pre-Islamic Central Asia.
symbols.credit: https://www.pinterest.it/pin/300826450093790824/

symbols.name: Panjakent Banquet Mural (detail)
symbols.location: Panjakent, Tajikistan (National Museum of Antiquities, Dushanbe)
symbols.desc: Detail of a banquet scene from the Panjakent murals; Sogdian elite halls paired feasting imagery with vegetal and tree motifs drawn from Iranian paradise symbolism.
symbols.credit: https://twitter.com/ccsahner/status/1133695337066110976?lang=fr

symbols.name: Simurgh-robed Delegate, Afrasiab Murals
symbols.desc: Detail from the Afrasiab 'Ambassadors' Painting' showing a delegate whose robe bears the simurgh — the mythical bird that perches on the tree of all seeds in Iranian cosmology.
symbols.credit: This image has been  extracted  from another file
symbols.artist: Painting: Unknown 7th century artist. Photographer: undetermined

symbols.name: The Felling of the Great Oak (Kalevala)
symbols.desc: Joseph Alanen's painting of the Kalevala's cosmic oak: a giant fells the monstrous oak that darkened the world, while tiny Väinämöinen marvels — the Finnish world-tree whose acorn shaded all the land.
symbols.credit: https://www.facebook.com/tampereentaidemuseo/photos/a.130671833629489/3450606881635951/

symbols.name: Khachkars of Dadivank Monastery
symbols.desc: Thirteenth-century Armenian khachkars at Dadivank Monastery; the cross-stone's wings sprout branches, palmettes and pomegranate vines so the cross becomes a flowering tree of life.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Gunungan / Kayon (Wayang Life-Tree Puppet)
symbols.desc: Wayang kulit gunungan or kayon ('life-tree') puppet of buffalo hide — the mountain-tree emblem planted at the start and end of every Javanese shadow-play, symbolizing the cosmic tree and the whole world.
symbols.credit: Wereldmuseum Amsterdam

symbols.name: Gunungan Kayon, Wayang Kulit Banjar
symbols.desc: Plate from an album of Banjar shadow puppets showing the gunungan/kayon, the tree-mountain figure that opens and closes a wayang performance as a symbol of the cosmos.
symbols.credit: http://repositori.kemdikbud.go.id/8166/

symbols.name: Coptic Textile: Dancers Among Plants
symbols.desc: Coptic wall-hanging fragment with dancers amid vines and plants — late-antique Egyptian weavers filled textiles with the flowering tree and vine-scroll motifs of paradise.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Roman Coin: Judaea Capta Palm Tree
symbols.location: Portable Antiquities Scheme find, United Kingdom
symbols.desc: Copper-alloy dupondius or as of Titus with the IUDAEA CAPTA reverse: a captive seated beneath a date palm — the Judean palm tree rendered as emblem of a conquered land on Roman coinage.
symbols.credit: https://finds.org.uk/database/ajax/download/id/218592  Catalog:  https://finds.org.uk/database/images/image/id/218592/recordtype/artefacts  Artefact:

symbols.name: Tlingit Totem Pole, Tongass Village Island
symbols.desc: Tlingit totem pole from Tongass Village Island topped by a brown bear; Tlingit poles are crest-tree monuments in which clan ancestry rises through the figures like the branches of a lineage tree.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: K'alyaan Totem Pole (Kiks.ádi Clan)
symbols.desc: The K'alyaan totem pole of the Tlingit Kiks.ádi Clan, erected to commemorate those lost in the 1804 Battle of Sitka; the carved cedar trunk carries the clan's raven-crest narrative upward.
symbols.credit: Transferred from   en.wikipedia   to Commons by  SchuminWeb  using  CommonsHelper .
symbols.artist: The original uploader was  Lordkinbote  at  English Wikipedia .

symbols.name: Kukui Tree (Hawaiian Enlightenment Tree)
symbols.desc: The kukui (Aleurites moluccanus), Hawaii's state tree: its oily nuts gave light, its wood made canoes, and it is revered as a kinolau body-form of Kamapua'a and an emblem of enlightenment and peace.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Kukui Trees of Iao Valley
symbols.desc: Photographic plate of kukui trees in Iao Valley from Hawaiian legend literature; the valley groves of kukui were sacred and associated with the demi-god Kamapua'a.
symbols.credit: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Legends_of_gods_and_ghosts_(Hawaiian_mythology).djvu/73

symbols.name: Codex Mendoza: Quauhnahuac 'Beside the Trees'
symbols.desc: Folio of the Codex Mendoza recording tribute from the province of Quauhnahuac ('Beside the Trees'), whose place-sign is a stylized tree with fruit — Nahuatl pictography naming towns by their trees.
symbols.credit: The Bodleian Libraries, University of Oxford

symbols.name: Tello Obelisk (Chavín Axis Mundi)
symbols.desc: The Tello Obelisk of Chavín de Huántar: a carved granite shaft covered with caimans, pumas, harpy eagles, snakes and plants — read as an axis mundi uniting the cosmic levels with edible and sacred species.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Serge (Yakut Ritual World-Tree Post)
symbols.location: Tabaginsky Cape, bank of the Lena River, Sakha Republic, Russia
symbols.desc: A serge — the Sakha ritual hitching-post carved from larch — standing on the Lena riverbank; in Yakut shamanism the serge marks the world-tree to which spirit-horses are tethered between the worlds.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Mongolian Ovoo (Shamanic Cairn-Tree)
symbols.desc: A Mongolian ovoo cairn hung with blue khadag scarves and a central tree-pole; the ovoo marks the axis where mountain and sky spirits are propitiated in Mongol shamanic culture.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Naxi Dongba Ovoo, Lijiang
symbols.desc: A Naxi Dongba 'MaNi hillock' ovoo near Lijiang, combining Naxi cult practices with the cairn-and-tree axis; Dongba cosmology centers on a sacred tree at the world's navel.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Tree of Life Mosaic, Hisham's Palace, Jericho
symbols.desc: The famous 'Tree of Life' mosaic in the audience hall of Hisham's Palace: two gazelles graze beneath a jeweled tree while a lion attacks the other — paradise and mortality set in tesserae.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Arbre de l'Oubli (Tree of Forgetting), Ouidah
symbols.desc: The bronze 'Tree of Forgetting' monument on the Slave Route at Ouidah, around which captives were made to circle so they would forget their homeland — a dark tree of memory and passage.
symbols.credit: Own work

symbols.name: Iznik Prunus Blossom Tile (Saz Style)
symbols.desc: Iznik ceramic tile with a flowering prunus branch — the Ottoman saz repertoire that transformed the Chinese tree-of-life motif into blossoming sap-vine ornament across mosques and palaces.
symbols.credit: Own work
